findings.description: storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, so the RDS MySQL instance's underlying EBS storage, snapshots and automated backups are stored unencrypted, exposing database contents if the storage layer is accessed.

publicly_accessible = true assigns a public endpoint to the RDS instance, making the MySQL service reachable from the internet subject only to the attached security group, which greatly widens the attack surface for credential brute force and exploitation.
The master username is hard-coded to the predictable default 'admin', which combined with a public endpoint makes credential guessing/brute-force attacks materially easier.

The master password is supplied through var.password, which is stored in plaintext in Terraform state (and likely in tfvars/CI variables) rather than being sourced from Secrets Manager or generated with manage_master_user_password, risking credential leakage.
iam_database_authentication_enabled is not enabled, so access relies solely on a static master password with no centralized IAM-based authentication or short-lived tokens.

deletion_protection is unset (defaults to false) and skip_final_snapshot is true, so the database and all its data can be destroyed with no recoverable snapshot by any principal with RDS delete permissions.
enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports is not configured, so MySQL audit, error and general logs are not shipped off-instance, hindering detection and forensic investigation of unauthorized database access.

The inline role policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", giving any principal assuming this role (the EC2 instance via aws_iam_instance_profile.ec2profile) full control over all S3 buckets, EC2 resources and RDS databases in the account. This violates least privilege and creates a direct privilege-escalation and data-exfiltration path if the instance is compromised.

The egress rule allows all protocols and all ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database/app security group, providing no outbound network segmentation and enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised host.

MySQL port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR rather than to the specific application security group, so every instance in the VPC (including any publicly exposed hosts) can reach the database directly.

The EC2 user_data script embeds the RDS master username and the plaintext database password (var.password) into a PHP include file. EC2 user data is retrievable by anyone able to reach the instance metadata service (including via SSRF from the hosted PHP app) and is stored unencrypted in the instance description, leaking the database credentials.

No metadata_options block is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled. Combined with an attached IAM instance profile and a public-facing PHP application, a server-side request forgery could retrieve role credentials and the credential-bearing user data.

No root_block_device or ebs_block_device configuration with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance volumes (which store the dbinfo.inc file containing the database password) may be unencrypted at rest.

The bootstrap script installs and starts httpd serving the employee data application over plain HTTP only, with no TLS configuration, so submitted names and addresses and query results traverse the network in cleartext.

dbinfo.inc containing the plaintext DB password is placed under /var/www/inc, inside the web server document root tree; a path traversal or misconfigured alias could serve the credentials file directly.
